children: slipped in premarket trading on Tuesday after the company announced plans to discontinue the development of its dwarfism therapy Voxzogo for Noonan syndrome, a rare genetically driven developmental disorder.

According to a federal register on clinical studies, the San Rafael, California-based biotech has been evaluating the safety and efficacy of the injection in a mid-stage trial for children with Noonan syndrome.

“BioMarin made this decision after assessing a number of factors, including the feasibility of the study and the current treatment landscape for children with Noonan syndrome,” the company said in a regulatory filing on Tuesday.
clarified that the decision did not stem from any safety or efficacy concerns related to Voxzogo.

Approved in the U.S. for achondroplasia, a genetic disorder characterized by short stature and disproportionate growth, Voxzogo is expected to generate $1,000M - $1,050M in revenue for the company this year, up 11% YoY

title: BioMarin halts studies for Voxzogo in Noonan syndrome
